holdout.note: in-sample 63.8% vs out-of-sample 66.7% (+/- 7.0% s.e.); MAE 12.15 -> 13.16. The signal holds out of sample.

correlations.what_it_is: Pearson r between the final margin and the final combined score, over all 183 games.
correlations.why_it_matters: The raw same-game relationship. If it were large, a spread leg and a total leg could never be priced independently.
correlations.note: not significant at this sample size

correlations.what_it_is: Pearson r between (actual margin - our predicted margin) and (actual total - our predicted total). This isolates the co-movement the model did not already price in.
correlations.why_it_matters: This is the number a same-game parlay needs: it is the correlation of the two legs' errors, so it is what turns a product of probabilities into a joint probability.
correlations.note: not significant at this sample size

correlations.what_it_is: Phi coefficient between the two binary legs priced against our own numbers (home covers our margin, and the total beats our total).
correlations.why_it_matters: Directly multiplies into a two-leg price. At rho = 0 a 0.50 x 0.50 parlay is 25.0%; the measured value says what it actually is.
correlations.note: not significant at this sample size

correlations.quantity: residual margin, game A vs game B on the same date
correlations.what_it_is: Pearson r between the margin residuals of every pair of games sharing a date.
correlations.why_it_matters: Cross-game parlays assume legs are independent. This is the test of that assumption on our own residuals.
correlations.note: not significant at this sample size

correlations.quantity: player points vs rebounds (same player, same game)
correlations.what_it_is: The within-player correlation a points+rebounds combo must price.
correlations.why_it_matters: Every one of these multiplies into a prop-combo price, and guessing any of them is how a combo is mispriced.
correlations.note: nba.com/stats player pages render season aggregates only for this client. Required for: minutes distributions, prop bet probabilities, injury replacement modelling.

gates.name: Source class
gates.requirement: Every input field resolves to an official NBA page or the official injury PDF.
gates.measured: 30 teams + 167 finals, each carrying an nba.com URL

gates.name: Completeness (team-level strategies)
gates.requirement: No required team-level input is blank.

gates.name: Sample floor
gates.requirement: Every team has at least 10 official games behind its rating before it is graded.
gates.measured: smallest prior sample feeding any published prediction: 16 games

gates.name: Estimator agreement
gates.requirement: Two independent ratings (net points per game; NetRtg per 100 possessions) must imply spreads within 2.0 points.

gates.name: Total-estimator agreement
gates.requirement: The points-based total and the independent pace x efficiency total must stay within 6.0 points.
gates.measured: largest gap across the 27-game slate: 4.04 pts (threshold 6.00)

gates.name: Market price present
gates.requirement: A dated, sourced price for the exact line must exist before anything is staked.
gates.measured: 0 prices in the repository; no odds feed is connected

gates.name: Backtest with settlement
gates.requirement: At least 300 settled bets of the strategy's own signals.

gates.name: Out-of-sample holdout
gates.requirement: Signals must hold on the last 30% of game-dates, having been built only on the earlier ones.
gates.measured: in-sample 63.8% vs out-of-sample 66.7% (+/- 7.0% s.e.); MAE 12.15 -> 13.16. The signal holds out of sample.

gates.name: Luck screen
gates.requirement: No strategy may lean on a team whose record sits outside the luck noise band (|z| > 1.96).

gates.name: Correlation honesty
gates.requirement: No parlay may be priced by multiplying legs unless the leg correlation is measured or bounded.

gates.name: Freshness
gates.requirement: Inputs must be dated within 24h of the slate and the injury report within its filing window.

gates.name: No look-ahead
gates.requirement: No input timestamped after the decision time may enter that decision.

strategies.name: Model side (moneyline, all games)
strategies.rule: Back the team our originated margin favours, priced at p = Phi(pred_margin / sigma_m).

strategies.name: Model total vs league average
strategies.rule: Take the over when our originated total clears the league-average total (227.5), priced at Phi((pred_total - ref) / sigma_t).

strategies.name: Model side, |margin| >= 5 pts
strategies.rule: S1 restricted to games where the two ratings disagree by at least 5 points, i.e. where the signal is loudest.

strategies.name: Road side when model fades home by 3+
strategies.rule: Back the road team only when our number makes the home team an underdog of 3 points or more. Tests whether the market's home bias is a real edge or a story.

strategies.name: Same-game parlay: side + total
strategies.rule: In every game take our side and our total as a two-leg parlay. Priced with the measured same-game correlation, not with a product of marginals.
strategies.base_rate_meaning: the joint probability this strategy printed

strategies.name: Cross-game parlay: two model sides
strategies.rule: Pair the two loudest side signals on a date into one two-leg parlay, priced as a product. Tests the independence assumption directly.
strategies.base_rate_meaning: the joint probability this strategy printed

strategies.name: Player prop / prop combo
strategies.rule: Price a player's points, rebounds and assists, and their combos, against a posted line. Requires a per-game minutes distribution and a within-player correlation; neither is reachable, so no bet is ever generated.

baselines.baseline: back the better prior win percentage
baselines.note: ties in prior W-L are skipped, not guessed

baselines.baseline: back the better prior average point differential
baselines.note: a scoring-margin prior, the strongest of the three

skill_attribution.note: A paired comparison needs the same games scored by both rules. The lab's S1 scores every game; the baselines skip ties, so the paired set is the intersection and both sides of the pairing are published with it.

headline_vs_win_pct_baseline.baseline: back the better prior win percentage
headline_vs_win_pct_baseline.verdict: the model's accuracy is not distinguishable from the favourite prior on the games where they disagree

headline_vs_margin_baseline.baseline: back the better prior average point differential
headline_vs_margin_baseline.verdict: the model's accuracy is not distinguishable from the scoring-margin prior on the games where they disagree

skill_attribution.why_this_matters: S1 backs the side its own ratings favour, and its ratings are built from the same results a reader can see. So the honest question is not 'is 64.7% better than 50%' - of course it is, favourites win - but 'is it better than simply backing the favourite'. The discordant-game test answers that, and it needs far fewer games than the 300-bet bar because only the disagreements carry information.

leaderboard.metric: log-loss (a proper scoring rule: honest probabilities beat lucky ones)

ranked.name: Road side when model fades home by 3+

reward_pool.allocation: 50 to rank 1, 30 split across ranks 2-4, 20 held in escrow for out-of-sample validation
reward_pool.status: UNFUNDED — no strategy is rank-eligible while gates G6, G7 fail

parlay_pricing.method: bivariate normal upper quadrant, deterministic 400-point quadrature

rows.legs: a strong side with a mild total

parlay_pricing.reading: At the measured rho of +0.0393 the joint is close to the product, but the 95% interval on rho runs -0.1133 to +0.1900 — wide enough that the honest statement is 'we do not know this correlation precisely enough to price a same-game parlay', not 'the legs are independent'. A two-leg price quoted from the product is therefore a guess with a known error bar, and the site withholds it rather than print the guess.
